//ConnectionStrings: No password here on purpose — a credential committed to the repo is a credential leaked.
In Docker, compose supplies ConnectionStrings__LineOps from .env.
For host-side `dotnet run`, supply the password out of band, either:
or: dotnet user-secrets set ConnectionStrings:LineOps '<full connection string>'
Npgsql also honours the standard PGPASSWORD environment variable.

//Sports: Leagues the scheduler polls. Listing any narrows to exactly those — the list replaces
the default rather than adding to it. Empty falls back to the four majors.
//LinePolling: The line cadence is derived, not configured: LinePollPlanner divides what the provider
still allows today by the cost of one scan and spreads the rest over the hours left, so
the allotment is used without being exceeded. These are only the safety margins.
DailyReserve keeps a slice back so a manual pull late in the day is never refused —
the budget guard should be a backstop, not a routine outcome.

//Mode: Manual: lines are fetched only when an operator presses Pull lines. Scheduled also lets
the scheduler scan on the derived cadence. Manual is the default because unattended
spending on a metered feed should be switched on deliberately, not inherited.

//GamePasses: ESPN is fetched around games rather than at a fixed hour: the slate is refreshed when a
start is close enough that times, postponements and scratches still matter, and results
are pulled once a started game is old enough to have finished — then retried until it is.
A 22:00 finish used to wait until 09:00 to settle.
//ColdClone: What a fresh clone gets with no keys at all:
Schedules, teams, players, box scores — yes. ESPN is keyless (ADR 0011) and the MLB
Stats API is unauthenticated, and both are on by default, so the board fills with real
fixtures and real results without signing up for anything.
Prices — no. Every odds provider is a book market behind a key, so an unkeyed clone
has no odds source at all and price cells read as empty. That is not an outage: the
Ops panel's Odds feeds section names each provider and says why it is not running, and
the alert rules skip a source that has never run (ADR 0003). Nothing pages anyone.
To get prices, set Enabled=true and a key on OddsApiIo or TheOddsApi below — out of
band, never in this file. There used to be an offline demo source filling this gap; it
was removed, because fabricated prices sit in the same tables as real ones and every
//OddsApiIo: The free odds feed. Stats come from ESPN; odds come from here, because ESPN carries one
book and a market needs several.
Set Enabled=true and supply the key out of band — never in this file:
Books cost nothing extra: a whole slate is two requests whatever the list, so the only
ceiling is the provider's free tier. A book outside the tier is quietly absent from the
response rather than an error, so an optimistic list degrades instead of failing.
//TheOddsApi: Second free tier, billed in credits rather than requests. Useful as a fallback or for
books the primary does not carry; the budget guard meters it either way.
//Espn: Unmetered and unauthenticated, which is why it is the only source history backfill
will use. RequestDelay paces every call it makes: a slate day is one request per
finished game, and a backfill walks hundreds of days.
//Backfill: Walks past days to build history the daily schedule would take months to accumulate.
Sources here are advisory: HistoryBackfillService admits unmetered providers only and
refuses metered ones whatever this names, so a backfill cannot spend anyone's quota.
Enabled=false by default — the operator starts it from the History window, because a
few thousand requests against a courtesy endpoint should be a decision, not a default.
Scoped to MLB, the only sport in season. Since pins the walk to opening day rather than
a rolling day count, which would cover a different stretch every time it ran. Add the
other leagues to Sports as their seasons start.
//OddsRetention: Odds are working state until first pitch and one permanent number afterwards.
HistoryFloor is the date the policy took effect: no scan from before it is kept,
promoted or not, because it can no longer become a closing line.

//Observability: Off by default: a cold clone should not spend its first run retrying a connection to a
collector nobody started. Compose turns it on and points it at the Aspire dashboard.
The KPI gauges are registered either way — they cost one query every 30s and are what
makes the reliability layer readable by tooling that knows nothing about this project.
